# Interchange

## `AssociatedFile`

```python
AssociatedFile(
    document: Document,
    host_getter: Callable[[], Dictionary],
    item_id: tuple[int, int],
    index: int = 0,
    *,
    host_requires_2_0: bool = False,
    single_key: str | None = None,
)
```

Live handle on an `AFFileSpecification` dictionary (ISO 32000-2 §14.13).

Properties read the current version of the document, and assigning
`filename`, `data`, `media_type`, `relationship`,
`description`, `created`, or `modified` edits the file
specification or embedded stream in one transaction. Once removed from its
host, the handle raises `StaleObjectError`, and works again if undo
restores it.

### `AssociatedFile.xref`

```python
AssociatedFile.xref: int
```

The indirect object number of the file specification, or `0` when direct.

### `AssociatedFile.obj`

```python
AssociatedFile.obj: Dictionary
```

The `AFFileSpecification` dictionary as a low-level handle.

### `AssociatedFile.filename`

```python
AssociatedFile.filename: str
```

The file name (`/UF`, falling back to `/F`); never empty.

Settable.

### `AssociatedFile.data`

```python
AssociatedFile.data: bytes
```

Or replace the decoded bytes of the embedded file stream (bounded at 64 MiB).

Settable.

### `AssociatedFile.media_type`

```python
AssociatedFile.media_type: str
```

The MIME media type stored on the stream's `/Subtype`.

Settable.

### `AssociatedFile.relationship`

```python
AssociatedFile.relationship: AssociatedFileRelationship | str
```

`/AFRelationship` (`AssociatedFileRelationship` or custom name).

Settable.

### `AssociatedFile.description`

```python
AssociatedFile.description: str | None
```

Return, set, or delete the optional file description (`/Desc`).

Settable.

### `AssociatedFile.created`

```python
AssociatedFile.created: str | None
```

Return, set, or delete `/Params /CreationDate` as a PDF date string.

Settable.

### `AssociatedFile.modified`

```python
AssociatedFile.modified: str | None
```

`/Params /ModDate` as a PDF date string.

Settable.

### `AssociatedFile.size`

```python
AssociatedFile.size: int
```

`/Params /Size`, or `-1` when absent.

## `AssociatedFileRelationship`

Semantic relationship of an associated file to its host object (`/AFRelationship`, Table 44).

Members: `SOURCE`, `DATA`, `ALTERNATIVE`, `SUPPLEMENT`, `ENCRYPTED_PAYLOAD`, `FORM_DATA`, `SCHEMA`, `UNSPECIFIED`.

## `AssociatedFiles`

```python
class AssociatedFiles(Sequence[AssociatedFile])
AssociatedFiles(
    document: Document,
    host_getter: Callable[[], Dictionary],
    *,
    host_requires_2_0: bool = False,
    prepare_host: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
)
```

Live sequence of `AssociatedFile` handles in a host's `/AF` array (ISO 32000-2 §14.13).

Exposed on `Document.associated_files`, `Page.associated_files`,
`StructureElement.associated_files`, `Annotation.associated_files`,
and `DocumentPart.associated_files`. Deleting the last entry removes
`/AF` from the host dictionary so `ArrayOfAFFileSpecifications` is never empty.

### `AssociatedFiles.__getitem__`

```python
AssociatedFiles.__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> AssociatedFile | list[AssociatedFile]
```

Return one `AssociatedFile`, or a list for a slice.

### `AssociatedFiles.__len__`

```python
AssociatedFiles.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of associated files on this host.

### `AssociatedFiles.__iter__`

```python
AssociatedFiles.__iter__() -> Iterator[AssociatedFile]
```

Iterate over the host's `AssociatedFile` handles.

### `AssociatedFiles.__bool__`

```python
AssociatedFiles.__bool__() -> bool
```

Return whether the host has at least one associated file.

### `AssociatedFiles.__delitem__`

```python
AssociatedFiles.__delitem__(index: int | slice)
```

Delete one associated file or a slice, removing `/AF` when empty.

### `AssociatedFiles.clear`

```python
AssociatedFiles.clear()
```

Remove all associated files from this host and delete `/AF`.

### `AssociatedFiles.add`

```python
AssociatedFiles.add(
    filename: str,
    data: bytes,
    *,
    media_type: str = 'application/octet-stream',
    relationship: AssociatedFileRelationship | str = AssociatedFileRelationship.UNSPECIFIED,
    description: str | None = None,
    created: str | datetime | None = None,
    modified: str | datetime | None = None,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> AssociatedFile
```

Embed `data` as an associated file on this host and return its handle.

## `DeveloperExtension`

```python
DeveloperExtension(
    prefix: str,
    base_version: str,
    extension_level: int,
    url: str | None = None,
    extension_revision: str | None = None,
)
```

A developer or ISO extension entry in `Catalog['Extensions']` (ISO 32000-2 §7.12).

`prefix` is the registered developer prefix (or `"ISO_"` for ISO
technical specifications in `ISO_EXTENSIONS`), `base_version` is
`"1.7"` or `"2.0"`, and `extension_level` identifies the extension
number. `url` and `extension_revision` record PDF 2.0 extension
metadata and are populated or checked automatically for `"ISO_"` entries.

## `DocumentPart`

```python
DocumentPart(document: Document, xref: int, generation: int = 0)
```

Live handle on an indirect `DPart` node in `Document.parts` (ISO 32000-2 §14.12).

Leaf parts span a contiguous range of pages (`start_page` through
`end_page`); branch parts group child `DocumentPart` handles in
`/DParts`. Metadata lives in `dpm` (never `/Metadata`), and files
in `associated_files`. A deleted handle raises `StaleObjectError`
and recovers on undo.

### `DocumentPart.document`

```python
DocumentPart.document: Document
```

The owning `Document`.

### `DocumentPart.xref`

```python
DocumentPart.xref: int
```

The indirect object number of this `DPart` dictionary.

### `DocumentPart.obj`

```python
DocumentPart.obj: Dictionary
```

The `DPart` dictionary in the low-level object model.

### `DocumentPart.parent`

```python
DocumentPart.parent: DocumentPart | None
```

The parent `DocumentPart`, or `None` for the root `DPart`.

### `DocumentPart.children`

```python
DocumentPart.children: tuple[DocumentPart, ...]
```

The direct child `DocumentPart` handles in `/DParts` order.

### `DocumentPart.start_page`

```python
DocumentPart.start_page: Page | None
```

The starting `Page` of a leaf part, or `None` on a branch.

Settable.

### `DocumentPart.end_page`

```python
DocumentPart.end_page: Page | None
```

The ending `Page` of a leaf part (defaults to `start_page`), or `None`.

Settable.

### `DocumentPart.pages`

```python
DocumentPart.pages: tuple[Page, ...]
```

All `Page` handles spanned by this leaf or branch subtree in document order.

### `DocumentPart.dpm`

```python
DocumentPart.dpm: dict[str, Any] | None
```

Return, replace, or delete the document part metadata dictionary (`/DPM`).

Settable.

### `DocumentPart.associated_files`

```python
DocumentPart.associated_files: AssociatedFiles
```

The `/AF` associated files of this document part (PDF 2.0).

### `DocumentPart.add_child`

```python
DocumentPart.add_child(
    start_page: Page | int,
    end_page: Page | int | None = None,
    *,
    dpm: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> DocumentPart
```

Add and return an indirect leaf `DocumentPart` child under this node in one transaction.

If this node was previously a leaf placeholder, `/Start` and `/End`
are cleared when `/DParts` receives the new child so Arlington's
branch/leaf invariant holds throughout.

### `DocumentPart.delete`

```python
DocumentPart.delete()
```

Remove this part and its subtree, pruning empty ancestor branches and `DPartRoot`.

```python
DocumentPartAction(part: DocumentPart)
```

An action that jumps to a `DocumentPart` (`/S /GoToDp`, ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.5, PDF 2.0).

## `Extensions`

```python
class Extensions(Mapping[str, tuple[DeveloperExtension, ...]])
Extensions(document: Document)
```

Live container for `Catalog['Extensions']` keyed by developer prefix (ISO 32000-2 §7.12).

Every dictionary and array written under `Catalog['Extensions']` is stored
directly as Arlington's `fn:MustBeDirect()` requires. Indexing by prefix
returns a tuple of `DeveloperExtension` records, `all` returns
every declared extension in order, and removing the last entry deletes
`Catalog['Extensions']`.

### `Extensions.__getitem__`

```python
Extensions.__getitem__(prefix: str) -> tuple[DeveloperExtension, ...]
```

Return the extensions registered under `prefix`, or raise `KeyError`.

### `Extensions.__iter__`

```python
Extensions.__iter__() -> Iterator[str]
```

Iterate over the declared developer prefixes in dictionary order.

### `Extensions.__len__`

```python
Extensions.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of declared developer prefixes.

### `Extensions.__contains__`

```python
Extensions.__contains__(item: object) -> bool
```

Return whether `item` is a declared prefix string or `DeveloperExtension`.

### `Extensions.__bool__`

```python
Extensions.__bool__() -> bool
```

Return whether the document declares at least one developer extension.

### `Extensions.all`

```python
Extensions.all() -> tuple[DeveloperExtension, ...]
```

Return all declared `DeveloperExtension` entries across every prefix.

### `Extensions.add`

```python
Extensions.add(extension: DeveloperExtension)
```

Add `extension` under its prefix in one transaction.

### `Extensions.remove`

```python
Extensions.remove(extension: DeveloperExtension)
```

Remove `extension` in one transaction, or raise `ValueError` when absent.

### `Extensions.__delitem__`

```python
Extensions.__delitem__(prefix: str)
```

Remove all extensions under `prefix` in one transaction, or raise `KeyError`.

### `Extensions.clear`

```python
Extensions.clear()
```

Remove `Catalog['Extensions']` in one transaction.

```python
ISO_EXTENSIONS = {

```

Canonical `(url, extension_revision)` metadata for registered ISO/TS extensions (ISO 32000-2 §7.12).

## `PieceData`

```python
PieceData(last_modified: str, private: Any = None)
```

One application's entry in a `/PieceInfo` page-piece dictionary (ISO 32000-2 Table 351).

`last_modified` is a PDF date string (`"D:..."`), and `private` holds
the application's private data dictionary, array, stream, or primitive.

## `PieceInfo`

```python
class PieceInfo(MutableMapping[str, PieceData])
PieceInfo(document: Document, host_getter: Callable[[], Dictionary], *, is_page: bool)
```

Live `MutableMapping` over `Catalog['PieceInfo']` or `PageObject['PieceInfo']` (ISO 32000-2 §14.5).

Writing promotes the document to PDF 1.4 on the catalog (ensuring trailer
`/Info` carries `/ModDate`) or PDF 1.3 on a page (updating
`PageObject['LastModified']`). Removing the last entry deletes
`/PieceInfo` from the host dictionary.

### `PieceInfo.__getitem__`

```python
PieceInfo.__getitem__(name: str) -> PieceData
```

Return the `PieceData` for application `name`, or raise `KeyError`.

### `PieceInfo.__setitem__`

```python
PieceInfo.__setitem__(name: str, value: PieceData)
```

Store `value` under `name` in one transaction.

### `PieceInfo.set`

```python
PieceInfo.set(
    name: str,
    private: object = None,
    *,
    last_modified: str | None = None,
) -> PieceData
```

Create, store, and return a `PieceData` under `name` (defaulting `last_modified` to UTC now).

### `PieceInfo.__delitem__`

```python
PieceInfo.__delitem__(name: str)
```

Remove application `name` from `/PieceInfo`, deleting `/PieceInfo` when empty.

### `PieceInfo.clear`

```python
PieceInfo.clear()
```

Remove `/PieceInfo` and all of its entries in one transaction.

### `PieceInfo.__iter__`

```python
PieceInfo.__iter__() -> Iterator[str]
```

Iterate over the application names stored in `/PieceInfo`.

### `PieceInfo.__len__`

```python
PieceInfo.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of valid application entries in `/PieceInfo`.

### `PieceInfo.__bool__`

```python
PieceInfo.__bool__() -> bool
```

Return whether `/PieceInfo` holds at least one entry.
